clue.text: As the PM, I replaced fellow on board

indicators.note: things replaced are put back in new positions, so the letters before it are rearranged

parts.note: the letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A prime minister is swapped out for a crewmate on board a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: A shipmate is a companion who sails with you, a fellow aboard the same vessel.

clue.text: Repeatedly pronounced present for statement of agreement

indicators.note: pronounced means spoken, so the word for present is taken by its sound

parts.note: present means here, said twice

explanation.surface: Someone keeps saying they are present, which comes across as agreeing.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is the traditional cry of approval in Parliament and at meetings.

clue.text: Similar pieces of music for gymnastic event

parts.note: parallel means alike or corresponding
bars are measures of music

explanation.surface: Matching tunes are chosen to accompany a gymnastics routine.
explanation.definitionFit: The parallel bars are a men's artistic gymnastics apparatus and the event performed on it.

clue.text: Joyce, for example, has car in US and runs over husband

indicators.note: over here means covering, so the car word sits around the husband

parts.note: auto is American for a car
H is the abbreviation for husband
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: James Joyce owns an American car and drives over his partner.
explanation.walkthrough: H goes inside AUTO, then R follows; the clue's order of pieces is loose, so the parse rests on the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: James Joyce, the Irish novelist of Ulysses, is an example of a writer.

clue.text: Moderate support for work of artist finally reduced by pound

indicators.note: reduced at the end by means the closing letter is taken away

parts.note: an easel holds a painter's canvas
L is the abbreviation for a pound sterling

explanation.surface: A painter's stand costs a pound less than expected.
explanation.walkthrough: The L removed from the end of EASEL is the pound.
explanation.definitionFit: To ease pain or tension is to moderate it, as a verb meaning lessen.

clue.text: Finishing courses, upset and under pressure

indicators.note: upset means turned upside down, which in a down clue reads the word from bottom to top

parts.note: desserts are the courses that end a meal

explanation.surface: Someone completing their training is anxious and tense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Finishing courses' suggests education; it is the end of a dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: Stressed means strained or tense, as someone under pressure feels.

clue.text: Capital on the Continent used by entrepreneur, often

indicators.note: used by means the answer is taken from inside the following words

parts.note: letters running across the two words

explanation.surface: A businessman often spends money in mainland Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: Capital is money, not a city.
explanation.definitionFit: The euro is the currency, the money or capital, of most countries of mainland Europe.

clue.text: Chic, getting tangled up with that small talk

indicators.note: things tangled up are knotted and disordered, so the letters are mixed together

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A stylish person gets caught up in idle gossip.
explanation.definitionFit: Chitchat is light informal conversation, a synonym for idle chatter.

clue.text: Everybody used their brains — not reaching conclusions, however

indicators.note: failing to reach the end means each of the two words stops short of its final letter

parts.note: everybody is all
to use one's brains is to think

explanation.surface: Everyone thought hard but nobody got to an answer.
explanation.walkthrough: Both words lose their last letters, giving ALTHOUGH.
explanation.definitionFit: Although and however are both conjunctions or adverbs introducing a contrast or concession.

clue.text: Accompanied by piano, song for man and wife, for instance

parts.note: p is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly
an air is a tune or song

explanation.surface: A married couple sings a duet at the piano.
explanation.walkthrough: The song is accompanied by the piano, so P comes before AIR.
explanation.definitionFit: A married couple is an example of a pair, two people joined together.

clue.text: Sportsman's complaint? Trainer can cover it up

definitions.meaning: surface reading: a grumble voiced by a player, perhaps against a coach
setter's reading: a trainer is a sports shoe, which hides a fungal infection of the foot

explanation.walkthrough: The trainer looks like a coach hushing up a scandal, but it is a running shoe covering an itchy foot condition.
explanation.definitionFit: The condition is a fungal skin infection of the feet, named for sportspeople who catch it in changing rooms.

clue.text: Amiability as short day closes without punishment for pupil

parts.note: Fri is the short form of Friday

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the word for closes goes around the punishment

parts.note: closes means ends
lines are sentences a pupil is made to write out as punishment

explanation.surface: A teacher is friendly as a brief Friday ends with no detention.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' reads as 'lacking' but means outside. Lines are a traditional school punishment.
explanation.definitionFit: Friendliness is the quality of being warm and amiable.

clue.text: Announced poor marks, then was concerned about learner

parts.note: D and E are low grades in an exam

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word for concerned goes around the learner

parts.note: to care is to be concerned
L is the learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: Bad exam results were made public, worrying the student.
explanation.walkthrough: Poor marks are low exam grades, and learner is the L of a learner driver's plate.
explanation.definitionFit: To declare something is to announce it formally.

clue.text: French writer turned up damaging information, as follows

indicators.note: turned up means flipped upward, which in a down clue reads the word from the bottom

parts.note: mud is scandal or smears, as in mudslinging
taken as written

explanation.surface: A French author unearths scandal, described below.
explanation.definitionFit: Alexandre Dumas was the French novelist who wrote The Three Musketeers.

clue.text: Pain streaker runs without

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a sharp pain in the side
second meaning: a streaker runs without a ... on, completing the idiom

explanation.surface: A streaker sprints off, perhaps in pain from the exertion.
explanation.walkthrough: The second half is a fill-in-the-blank: someone naked is 'without a stitch on', a single bit of sewn clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A stitch is both a sudden side ache from running and a single loop of thread in clothing.

clue.text: Kind of examination, of the type that dentist does

definitions.text: of the type that dentist does
definitions.meaning: second meaning: relating to the mouth

explanation.surface: A dentist conducts a certain kind of check-up.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means both spoken, as in a viva test, and relating to the mouth, a dentist's domain.

clue.text: Players together after part of cricket match? It's not clear

indicators.note: after places the word for players together behind the cricket part

parts.note: an over is a set of six balls bowled from one end in cricket
the cast is the full company of actors

explanation.surface: A cricket team meets after part of the game, unsure of the result.
explanation.walkthrough: Players looks sporting next to cricket, but it means actors.
explanation.definitionFit: An overcast sky is cloudy, the opposite of clear weather.

clue.text: In short spell, I had easily dominated

indicators.note: something short is cut down, so the word for spell loses its last letter

parts.note: a spell is a period of time
I'd is the contraction of I had

explanation.surface: Someone admits that for a brief period they were a pushover.
explanation.definitionFit: A timid person lacks confidence and so is readily pushed around.

clue.text: Negotiate with a couple of partners in area

indicators.note: in means the preceding pieces sit inside the word for area

parts.note: a tract is an area of land
taken as written
North and South are partners at bridge

explanation.surface: Two business partners bargain in a region.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge the four players are named by compass points, and N and S play as partners.
explanation.definitionFit: To transact is to conduct or negotiate a piece of business.

clue.text: Cold-blooded animal's current temperature

parts.note: current in the sense of latest, new
T is the abbreviation for temperature

explanation.surface: A reptile's body temperature is being measured right now.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Current' tempts toward electricity (AC, I), but here it means up to date.
explanation.definitionFit: A newt is an amphibian, and amphibians are cold-blooded creatures.

clue.text: Haphazardly wore drab set of clothes

indicators.note: haphazardly means without order or plan, so the letters are scattered into a new sequence

parts.note: the letters taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone carelessly dressed in dull clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: A wardrobe can mean a person's whole collection of clothes, not just the cupboard.

clue.text: Mistakes in text are holding sailor back

indicators.note: back means the whole combination is read in the reverse direction
holding means keeping inside, so the sailor goes within the word are

parts.note: taken as written
tar is an old word for a sailor

explanation.surface: A proofreader finds errors in a text about a seaman.
explanation.walkthrough: Tar is an old nickname for a sailor; the reversal applies to the whole combination after the insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: Errata is the Latin plural for errors, used for a list of printing mistakes in a book.

clue.text: People of little importance for school of the future?

definitions.meaning: second meaning: young fish, which will one day form a school of adult fish

explanation.surface: Unimportant people are told they are the future of the school.
explanation.walkthrough: School here is a shoal of fish, not a place of learning; fry are newly hatched fish.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom for unimportant people, and literally means little young fish.

clue.text: Get out of carriage, say, that's on fire

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to step down from a vehicle

explanation.surface: Passengers are told to leave a carriage that is burning.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a verb for stepping off a train and an adjective meaning burning.

clue.text: Sample of people irritated by silly notices

parts.note: cross means annoyed

indicators.note: silly means foolish or muddled, so the letters of notices are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Members of the public are annoyed by foolish signs.
explanation.definitionFit: A cross-section is a representative sample drawn from all parts of a group.

clue.text: Finishes off solo in total disarray, just and no more

indicators.note: finishes means endings, so the closing letter of each word is kept

parts.note: the last letter of each of the four words

explanation.surface: A solo performer ends up in complete chaos.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Disarray' looks like an anagram signal but is just one of the four words supplying a final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Only means merely, nothing beyond what is stated.

clue.text: Amusing person, such as joker

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an eccentric, funny individual
second meaning: a joker belongs to a pack of playing ...

explanation.walkthrough: The joker seems to describe the amusing person, but it is the extra card in a deck.
explanation.definitionFit: A card is old slang for a witty character, and also a playing card, of which the joker is one.

clue.text: College, from middle of fifteenth century

indicators.note: middle of means only the central letter of the nine-letter word is kept

parts.note: the fifth of nine letters
a ton is a hundred, as a century is

explanation.surface: A college dates from the mid-1400s.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is true: Eton College was founded in 1440. 'Fifteenth century' looks like one phrase but splits into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Eton College is the famous English public school near Windsor.

clue.text: Sincere changes, inserting line that moderates report

indicators.note: inserting means putting the line inside the rearranged letters
changes means the letters of sincere are altered into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
L is the abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: An honest person changes, adding a line that tones down a written account.
explanation.walkthrough: Report here is the bang of a gun, not a document.
explanation.definitionFit: A silencer is a device fitted to a gun barrel to muffle the noise of the shot.

clue.text: Legal document about trial regarded as awful

indicators.note: about means going around, so the legal document wraps around the trial

parts.note: a deed is a legal document
a trial is a test

explanation.surface: A contract concerning a court case was thought terrible.
explanation.definitionFit: To detest something is to loathe it, so it is regarded as awful.
